issue.title: Pretty print of ```<script>``` in html causes extra lines to be added on each subsequent pretty print

labels.name: bug
labels.description: A confirmed bug, that we should fix

milestone.description: A planned future version of jsoup. Tag this milestone for breaking changes that were deprecated in 1.14.x.

repository.name: jsoup
repository.description: jsoup: the Java HTML parser, built for HTML editing, cleaning, scraping, and XSS safety.

issue.body: Take https://github.com/revelc/formatter-maven-plugin/blob/main/src/test/resources/someFile.html and add <script>doSomething();<script> to the file as a test.  Run the formatting over and over, watch it keep adding extra empty lines every time it encounters a script block with content.  I've been looking into this but have yet to find where this problem is coming from.  Any pointers to help debug and/or suggest where this might be fixed would be greatly appreciated.  This is pretty print and makes it hard to use formatter-maven-plugin to format when this is encountered.  Issues are present in latest master even though we are still using the older releases at the moment.

body:
Thanks! Have fixed this by checking in TextNode if the node is just a newline + empties, which can be safely whitespace normalized away. Effectively, this means if the parent element created an indent, if this TextNode (on re-parse) is the content of that indent, we should skip it.

This is a relatively new issue - in earlier versions of jsoup, these TextNodes (\n\s+) would have been dropped during parsing. We changed that to better preserve content when pretty printing was disabled, but that caused this knock-on impact.
